source_snapshot.message:
fix(view): scope the remap to the workspace, and serialise it

Follow-up to the review of this PR. The guard itself held against every
probe I could think of — Origin: null, file://, data:, userinfo tricks,
trailing-dot Host, short-form IPv4, absolute-form request lines, path
traversal, percent-encoding — so what follows is about what happens
*after* a request is allowed through.

**The remap mapped the server's cwd.** `ix view start` spawns the
detached server with no cwd option, so it inherits wherever it was
launched, and remap ran `ix map .` there. `--all` deliberately does not
require the cwd to be a workspace (view.ts opts out of resolveWorkspaceId
entirely), and CLAUDE.md documents `ix view start --all --no-open` as the
normal invocation — so starting it from a home directory turned one click
into an ingest of the whole of it. The workspace root is now resolved by
`ix view start`, by the same lookup that produces the x-ix-workspace
header, and baked into the script; an unscoped view answers 409 instead
of falling back to the cwd.

That reach was not limited to the button. The Origin check accepted any
loopback hostname on any port, and a simple POST needs no preflight, so
any page served on another localhost port could trigger it. Origin must
now match this server's port too.

**Nothing serialised the maps.** execFile is asynchronous: 12 concurrent
POSTs started 12 concurrent `ix map` runs over the same workspace,
measured. The client's in-flight flag is per-tab, so two tabs were enough.
One at a time now, 409 while busy.

**MAP_MAIN is baked in rather than re-derived.** `resolve(DIST, "..",
"..")` only yields IX_HOME for the installed layout; findCompassDist's
dev branch returns a repo path, from which the same arithmetic lands on a
file that never exists. It now comes from this module's own location at
generation time, which holds for both. The IX_VIEW_MAP_MAIN seam is
honoured only under NODE_ENV=test, so a shipped install cannot be
redirected to an arbitrary script through the environment.

`--silent` and an explicit maxBuffer: nothing reads that stdout, and the
default 1 MiB makes Node SIGTERM the child mid-map, surfacing as a 500
rather than as the truncation it is. Reachable only if the output ever
grows with the repo — today the tree render is capped at --max-items and
ingest prints a fixed summary — but the map does not need to render at
all. The request body is drained rather than left open for the map's
duration.

Two in bootstrap.sh, both pre-existing:

- The backticks in the docker warning were command substitutions, not
  quoting. The failure path re-ran `ix docker start`, then ran `ix doctor`
  and `ix status`, spliced their stdout into the message, and left the
  user with the command names stripped out of the advice.
- is_windows() had dropped MSYSTEM along with WSL_DISTRO_NAME, which the
  comment justified only for WSL. Restored; the WSL fix is untouched.

Tests move to src/cli/__tests__/ — tsconfig is include: ["src"], so at
their old path CI never type-checked them. They no longer leak a temp
directory per run or write a marker into the package root, and replacing
the server now awaits the old child's exit rather than re-binding the
port under it. 10 -> 13 tests; the three new ones each fail against a
mutant of the guard they cover.

735 tests pass; typecheck, lint and knip clean.
